FINITE COHERENT THERMAL PORTS AND A JOINT ATHERMALITY-BOUNDED MEMORY
1 November 2026. Solo construction and analytic proof candidate.
The inherited stationary/module and RX/RZ results have the completed internal
review recorded in the pinned current Astra sources. This new composition
and warm-start lemma have not received an independent audit. No novelty,
microscopic device, practical threshold or mission-level advance is asserted.

Purpose and actual gain
=======================
The earlier compact Ising block protects a quantum input only in a strong
logical-symmetry noise algebra. Here the code protects BOTH Pauli sectors.
Finite coherent controllers replace the engineered DATA dissipators of a
thermal memory by bounded-support HAMILTONIAN ports and ONE-SITE controller
thermal channels. The actual data/controller evolution is quantum and may
be strongly non-Markovian after the controllers are traced out. There is
no g/Gamma limit, no secular data-only generator and no nT implementation
error. The nominal product thermal encoder remains the reference encoder.

This is a different restricted model: it requires a common stationary
thermal REFERENCE for the WHOLE specified device, including its couplers
and controller reservoirs. It admits thermal creation and repair of every
single-qubit X,Y,Z error. It does not require an exact conserved logical
flip or declare one bare-qubit error type absent. Energy selectors remain
bounded-arity physical Hamiltonian primitives; no two-body compiler is proved.

1. Input thermal-code interface and existing result actually used
===============================================================
Let H_D=sum_(a=1)^m (I-S_a)/2 be a commuting Pauli stabilizer Hamiltonian
on n data qubits, with one logical qubit, check weight <=w, incidence <=D,
and bounded range/density in the supplied geometry. Fix ONE Pauli decoder
and its unitary recovery coordinates

Valid syndrome constraints and redundant checks are included in H_S; no
independently assignable syndrome oracle is assumed. Corrected logical
Paulis form the full matrix algebra on Q in these same coordinates.

FINITE THERMAL CONTROLLERS: ACTUAL COSTS, COMPARATORS AND SOURCE SCOPE
1 November 2026. All new work is local to this task. Earlier results are
unchanged. The new theorem is a solo analytic composition and correlated-
input extension; it does not inherit an audit by using audited premises.

What was already available before construction
==============================================
The supplied primary three-dimensional memory already addresses both
Pauli sectors under Gibbs-stationary local dynamics, using a thermal
encoding. Its proved lifetime construction uses the qualified recursive
random-embedding family. Its explicitly embedded variant leaves the full
lifetime proof for future work; efficient passive initialization is also
left open. These distinctions were read before selecting a new bridge.
 https://arxiv.org/html/2605.10943v1
 Relevant passages: sections1.1,1.2.4,1.3 and2.5, including theorem2.6.

The photonic-Ising proposal already combines cat and Ising protection.
Its leakage treatment includes idealized, toy and mean-field analyses;
its microscopic construction invokes Born-Markov/RWA and nonlinear
Josephson parity couplers. Section5 charges large photon-number-dependent
circuit scales. This is stronger than simply assuming a bare-qubit bias.
It still does not supply the full finite-controller/leakage certificate
needed for our transfer. The projection countermodel below tests an
inference, not the actual proposal.
 https://arxiv.org/html/2205.09767v3
 Relevant passages: main leakage discussion and supplemental sections4-5.

The stationary quantum-memory criterion is established prior machinery:
Chesi--Loss--Bravyi--Terhal (2010), as restated in theorem2.6 of the primary
3D paper. No invention of that criterion is claimed here. Its source is
 https://arxiv.org/abs/0907.2807
The primary restatement and current Astra module reconstruction were read;
the original2010 proof was not used as a separately reconstructed premise.

FINITE COHERENT CONTROLLERS FOR BOTH QUANTUM ERROR TYPES
1 November 2026. A completed solo construction/proof candidate and4 executed
controls. Prior spectral, generic-noise transfer and exact repetition-code
symmetry-breaking results remain unchanged.

The strongest existing starting point already protects both Pauli sectors:
the primary3D thermal code, and current Astra's internally reviewed fixed-
nominal-controller and ideal thermal-initializer results. Their actual
premises were retrieved from current public main and whole governing sources.
The new work concerns a different physical controller interface and
correlated-input/resource statement, not invention of the thermal code.

Constructed bridge
------------------
Replace each code-site thermal Pauli channel by exact energy-selected
coherent coupling to a finite controller level, with one-site paired
thermal loss/gain. The full device keeps the SAME product Gibbs reference
at any fixed finite coupling and reset rate. There is no controller
elimination, periodic reset, g/Gamma limit, or nT approximation debit.
The large-code model has nonzero X/Y/Z creation/repair paths and, nominally,
no conserved logical parity. It protects an unknown qubit/reference with
error <=C nT exp(-c n^alpha), while preserving the qualified3D geometry.

Added joint theorem
--------------------
For all initial Q/C/B/R correlations with auxiliary marginal
rho_CB<=M tau_CB, a single CPTP comparison map evolves the SAME C,B and
preserves Q. Its uniform reference-trace error is

             <=C nT sqrt(M p_bad).

Since p_bad<=C' exp(-c n^alpha), initial athermality log M below that
barrier retains a stretched-exponential interval. This is a constrained
joint input theorem, not an unconstrained diamond bound over all baths.
It charges accessible bath/controller energy, negentropy and correlations;
an untouched purification does not enlarge the marginal resource cost.

Exact remaining physical obstruction
-------------------------------------
Energy selectors are actual bounded-arity Hamiltonian primitives. They
cannot simply be replaced by bilinear couplers while keeping this proof's
product reference: a scoped Pauli-independence no-go is proved, including
the full five-qubit fixture, and its matched lowering ports require at
least four data sites. This is NOT a general two-body memory no-go.
